title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 23
paragraphs: So that is how it happened with respect to these things. At the same time Megabazus had arrived at the Hellespont bringing with him the Paeonians, and from there, after crossing the straits, came to Sardis. Now Histiaeus the Milesian was already busy fortifying with a wall the place he had asked for and received from Darius as a reward for keeping safe the bridge of boats—this place being what is called Myrcinus, lying along the bank of the river Strymon. Megabazus, perceiving what Histiaeus was doing, as soon as he came to Sardis with the Paeonians said to Darius: “O king, what is this you have done, granting permission to a Hellene—a skillful and cunning one—to found a city in Thrace in a place where there is abundant forest for shipbuilding and a great supply of wood for oars and silver mines, and great numbers both of Hellenes and barbarians living round about, who, when they get a leader, will do whatever he orders, day and night. Stop this man from doing this, then, so that you are not caught up in a domestic war; stop him by sending for him in a courteous way, but once you have him in your hands, arrange that he shall never again return to the land of the Hellenes.”
